task.assignment: Voices, C116: you pick whose own words carry the day
task.approach: Voices approach: this slice is a roster, a tip sheet, not your assignment — every citizen with a page on the record, one line each. You pick whose own words carry the day, and why. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

assignment.approach: Voices approach: this slice is a roster, a tip sheet, not your assignment — every citizen with a page on the record, one line each. You pick whose own words carry the day, and why. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

angleRead.name: Ines Sorensen
angleRead.text: I'm heading to Uptown to catch up with Tre Mingo about the Baylight fence line's progress and how it ties into the neighborhood's changing vibe. The A's season is over, but the impact of Mark Aitken's departure still lingers. I'll also try to touch base with Theo Banks and see if his perspective on the rent hikes dominating local conversations has shifted.
